newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia releases Black Panther activist.
newsitem.headline: Australia releases Black Panther activist.

text.p: Former U.S. Black Panther activist Lorenzo Ervin was released on Friday from a maximum security Australian jail after the government said it had denied Ervin his full rights before ordering him deported.
On leaving jail, Ervin called on Australian Prime Minister John Howard to apologise for his treatment.
"It is really a shame that a person cannot live down their political past," Ervin told reporters.
"I would say Mr Howard owes me an apology," he said.
The black human rights activist will on Monday attend an immigration department hearing to show cause why he should be allowed to stay in Australia.

Ervin was detained in Brisbane on Tuesday after the government ordered his deportation on grounds that he was not of good character, based on his conviction for hijacking an aircraft from the United States to Cuba in 1969.
But on Friday the government announced a surprise decision to reverse the order to cancel Ervin's visa.
Acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone said the government had reversed its decision because it had not granted Ervin "procedural rights" in the original decision.
"It (the government) has not backed down on this matter," Vanstone said in a statement.
"The decision today has no bearing on the real issue of this matter, namely, whether or not Mr Ervin is a person of good character," she said.

On Monday, Howard said he was shocked to hear Ervin had been allowed to enter Australia on July 4 and hoped he would be deported. On Tuesday, Vanstone cancelled Ervin's visa and ordered him detained and deported.
The minister said Ervin was not of good character and had falisified his immigration documents -- a charge Ervin denies.
Ervin unsuccessfully sought two new visas and took legal action in Australia's High Court, saying he had been denied natural justice.

Ervin's lawyer Terry Fisher said the government's decision on Friday was a "backdown" and a "major victory for free speech". Ervin was invited to Australia for a four-week speaking tour by anarchist group Angry People.
